To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is advantageous, from the point of view of the Josephson critical current, to measure the magnetic diffraction of planar junctions with a transverse magnetic rather than an inplane magnetic field.
a transverse magnetic diffraction pattern is more favorable for the observation of the Fraunhofer pattern than the in-plane magnetic diffraction pattern.

a transverse magnetic diffraction pattern is observed when the magnetic field is applied in a direction perpendicular to the plane of the planar Josephson junction, and that this pattern is different from the one observed with the field applied parallel to the plane of junction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of high quality Josephson junctions and arrays for the purpose of investigating the properties of superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs), the development of SQUID magnetometers and the study of the physics of Josephson junctions.

the development of new types of Josephson tunnel junction structures with improved characteristics for the fabrication of high-quality SQUID devices and for applications in quantum information processing.
the static properties of planar Nb-based Josephson tunnel junction with different geometry, critical current density, and junction size.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the critical current versus magnetic-field curves are better behaved in the transverse field.
a transverse field is preferable to an in-plane field in the case of high quality planar junctions with small junction size and high critical current density.

the use of a transverse magnetic-field configuration for Josephson tunnel junction characterization is advantageous in the sense that it is easier to obtain reproducible results and to obtain junctions with the highest possible critical current density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a transverse magnetic diffraction pattern can be obtained for junctions with any geometry and size.
the junction properties in a magnetic field can be optimized with a transverse magnetic diffraction pattern, and this is particularly important for junctions with high critical current densities.
it is advantageous for planar Josephson junctions to use a trans- verse field rather than an In-Plane field, especially for high critical current density junctions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transverse magnetic diffraction pattern in a planar Josephson junction is a direct measure of the critical current distribution across the junction.
a transverse field is more effective than an in-plane magnetic field in suppressing the Josephson effect.

in the case of a transverse field the junction magnetic diffraction pattern is not a superposition of the patterns in the two electrodes, as is the case for an in-plane field, and the junction critical current is determined by a single junction characteristic length.
